sourcesRead.title: Entropy-Aligned Decoding of LMs for Better Writing and Reasoning (Ahmed, Singh)
REAL Sampling: Boosting Factuality and Diversity of Open-Ended Generation via Asymptotic Entropy (Chang, Peng, Bansal, Ramakrishna, Chung; Amazon AGI)
The Effect of Sampling Temperature on Problem Solving in Large Language Models (Renze, Guven)
Surprisal reveals diversity gaps in image captioning and different scorers change the story (Ilinykh, Dobnik)
Look-back Decoding for Open-Ended Text Generation (Xu, Zhou, Celikyilmaz, Ma)

claims.claim: Ahmed and Singh state that the greedy heuristics inside current decoding algorithms introduce myopic distortions whose result is homogeneous, repetitive and incoherent sentences.
claims.source: Ahmed, Singh, 'Entropy-Aligned Decoding of LMs for Better Writing and Reasoning', arXiv:2601.01714v1 (2026)
claims.quote: yielding sentences that are homogeneous, repetitive
claims.modelEra: January 2026 preprint; base language model not named in the sections read; register measured: WritingPrompts stories and CNN/DailyMail summaries

claims.claim: Ahmed and Singh describe the existing truncation heuristics as ad hoc and grounded only in empirical observation rather than in a principled target.
claims.quote: these heuristics are often ad hoc, based
claims.modelEra: January 2026 preprint; register: creative writing, summarisation, mathematical reasoning

claims.claim: Ahmed and Singh measure that top-p, top-k and min-p all drift systematically away from the target cross-entropy even with tuned hyperparameters, so the entropy of their sampled text is persistently miscalibrated.
claims.quote: exhibit systematic bias away from the target entropy
claims.modelEra: January 2026 preprint; base model not named in the sections read; register measured: WritingPrompts and CNN/DailyMail

claims.claim: Ahmed and Singh report a win rate of 0 per cent for plain temperature sampling at tau equals 1.5 against min-p on the WritingPrompts story task, judged by ChatGPT-5 and averaged over ten seeds.
claims.modelEra: January 2026; judge is ChatGPT-5, not human raters; register measured: WritingPrompts story generation

claims.claim: Chang and colleagues state the nucleus sampling trade-off as a direct one, in which raising the p threshold raises diversity and lowers factuality.
claims.source: Chang, Peng, Bansal, Ramakrishna, Chung, 'REAL Sampling', arXiv:2406.07735v1 (2024)
claims.quote: higher p threshold in the nucleus (top-p) sampling increases the diversity but
claims.modelEra: 7B language models with a 70M forecasting model, June 2024; register measured: FactualityPrompts open-ended continuations

claims.claim: Renze and Guven found no statistically significant effect of sampling temperature between 0.0 and 1.0 on multiple-choice problem-solving accuracy.
claims.source: Renze, Guven, 'The Effect of Sampling Temperature on Problem Solving in Large Language Models', arXiv:2402.05201v3 (2024)
claims.quote: do not have a statistically significant impact on LLM performance
claims.modelEra: nine LLMs, temperatures 0.0 to 1.6, observation 2024; register measured: multiple-choice question answering, not prose

claims.claim: Renze and Guven's temperature result rests on nine language models crossed with five prompt-engineering techniques on a multiple-choice exam sampled from standard benchmarks.
claims.quote: nine popular LLMs with five prompt-engineering techniques
claims.modelEra: nine LLMs, 2024; register measured: multiple-choice question answering

claims.claim: Ilinykh and Dobnik measure that human image captions carry roughly twice the surprisal variance of five vision-and-language model caption sets when scored with a caption-trained n-gram model.
claims.source: Ilinykh, Dobnik, 'Surprisal reveals diversity gaps in image captioning', arXiv:2511.04754v1 (2025)
claims.quote: roughly twice the surprisal variance of models
claims.modelEra: five vision-and-language LLMs with greedy and nucleus decoding, November 2025; register measured: MSCOCO image captions, not prose fiction or archival text

claims.claim: Ilinykh and Dobnik report that rescoring the same captions with a general language model instead of a caption-trained one reverses the human-model surprisal-variance gap, so a single scorer can invert the conclusion.
claims.quote: on a single scorer can completely invert
claims.modelEra: five vision-and-language LLMs, November 2025; register measured: MSCOCO image captions

claims.claim: Xu and colleagues measure that as a loop sets in the minimum Kullback-Leibler divergence between the current step's distribution and the earlier steps' distributions falls towards zero, where a human continuation keeps it away from zero.
claims.source: Xu, Zhou, Celikyilmaz, Ma, 'Look-back Decoding for Open-Ended Text Generation', arXiv:2305.13477v2 (2023)
claims.quote: distribution distance with past gradually approaches 0
claims.modelEra: GPT2-XL and GPT-3 (ada-001, davinci-002), observation 2023; register measured: open-ended continuation and story generation

claims.claim: Xu and colleagues report that the coherence hypothesis behind confidence-following decoders does not always hold, since a greedy decoder rigorously following model confidence can produce incoherent sentences.
claims.quote: coherence hypothesis of pretrained LMs in prior
claims.page: Section 3, discussion of Table 1 degeneration examples
claims.modelEra: GPT2-XL and GPT-3 ada-001 and davinci-002, 2023; register measured: open-ended continuation

claims.claim: Xu and colleagues relay the induction-head account of Olsson and colleagues, prefix matching and copying, as a possible explanation of repetitive generation.
claims.confidenceReason: the mechanism is cited from Olsson et al. 2022, not measured in this paper
